pr_title: cryptenroll: Implement support for unlocking via FIDO2 tokens
pr_body:
This allows FIDO2 users to wipe out password slots and still be able to
enroll new key slots via systemd-cryptenroll. Note that when the user
wants to both unlock with a FIDO2 token and enroll a new FIDO2 token,
they cannot be set to automatic discovery. This is to safeguard against
confusion, because there will be multiple tokens connected to the system
when doing so -- and we require users to explicitly confirm which one to
use for unlocking and which one to use for enrollment.

Addresses #20230 for the FIDO2 case.
pr_comments:
commit msg should probably reference #20230.

(i guess we can close #20230 once there's similar logic for unlocking via pkcs#11 tokens in place, hence just reference that issue, don't add "Closes:" for it just yet)
Fixed an extra empty line in cryptenroll-fido2.c and it seems that the ubuntu CIs are failing for unrelated reasons again.

Sorry for all the noise, last minor change: added proper error logging in `load_volume_key_fido2()` when `acquire_fido2_key_auto()` returns `-EAGAIN`, because that function expects callers to try again and/or prompt the user to try again. In cryptenroll we just need to pass this message to the user directly and abort.

By the way, @bluca please do not set #20230 to be auto-closed when this PR is merged. That issue needs at least PKCS#11 unlocking to be also implemented in cryptenroll. This PR only deals with FIDO2, which is arguably the more common use-case but that issue does cover all types of tokens.

issue_context.title: cryptenroll: supports use of pkcs11 token to initiate enrollment process
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
`systemd-cryptenroll` only accepts passphrases to initiate enrollment. So once your password or recovery key is wiped, you can no longer use `systemd-cryptenroll`.

```
# systemd-cryptenroll --wipe-slot=all --fido2-device=auto /dev/sdb1
🔐 Please enter current passphrase for disk /dev/sdb1: ****                    
Initializing FIDO2 credential on security token.
👆 (Hint: This might require confirmation of user presence on security token.)
🔐 Please enter security token PIN: ****                    
Generating secret key on FIDO2 security token.
👆 In order to allow secret key generation, please confirm presence on security token.
New FIDO2 token enrolled as key slot 1.
Wiped slot 0.
# systemd-cryptenroll --recovery-key /dev/sdb1
🔐 Please enter current passphrase for disk /dev/sdb1: ****                    
Password not correct, please try again.
```

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Get every enrolled types and tries to unlock the volume with it. Something like `systemd-homed` based user authentication.
comments:
The man page added with the tool (in https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/17741) is also a bit misleading, especially this example:

> [...] Combining wiping and enrollment may also be used to replace enrollments of different types, for example for changing from a PKCS#11 enrollment to a FIDO2 one:
>
> `systemd-cryptenroll /dev/sda1 --wipe-slot=pkcs11 --fido2-device=auto`

A warning should be added that you can't easily rotate ex: your FIDO2 key if the password is removed.
@gibeom-gwon so in case of wiping password and setting fido2/tpm there is really no way to change configuration at all? Does it technically possible or I have lost this ability forever?
@L11R In the usual way, you can't. But I was able to find the binary password by debugging systemd-crypt.
@gibeom-gwon is it hard to obtain it? Don't want to reinstall the system :\

@L11R It's not so hard if you can use GDB. I forgot the exact way, but it was something like this:

1. Debug `/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-cryptsetup` with GDB.
2. Set the breakpoint to `crypt_activate_by_volume_key`. This is the cryptsetup API. Third argument is the key pointer and fourth is the key length.
3. `systemd-cryptsetup` usage is like this: `systemd-cryptsetup attach VOLUME SOURCEDEVICE [PASSWORD] [OPTIONS]`. Set the argument and run.
4. When the breakpoint is hit, finds the key and saves it to a file as a binary.
5. Use the file as a key file and add the password using `cryptsetup luksAddKey`.
@gibeom-gwon thanks! Sounds not so hard, will give it a try. But devs should definitely fix this or at least add the warning.

@gibeom-gwon thank you again! I accessed my key! But in my case I got key here: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v249/src/cryptsetup/cryptsetup.c#L874
I have printed base64_encoded variable and it was a passphrase.
@L11R I'm glad to hear that! I think I misremembered the function I used.

so setups where you *only* have pkcs11/tpm2/fido2 keys enrolled and nothing else are not well supported, because cryptenroll only accepts regular passphrases or recovery keys as requirements for enrolling new keys. This issue is about supporting pkcs11/tpm2/fido2 for that too, but it's not there yet.

(Note though that the way pcs11/tpm2/fido2 is put together in systemd-cryptenroll/systemd-cryptsetup is that we'll never pass the binary key as is to LUKS, but will always base64 encode it, and pass the encoded form. This means you ultimately always have a fallback option: you could type in the base64 encoded string where you get asked for a passphrase. Of course, that isn't fun though, since the string is rather long and hard to type.)

I'll prep a patch that for now mentions explicitly that doing pkcs11/tpm2/fido2-only setups is not precisely easy right now if you ever intend to roll-over enrolled keys.

I ran into the problem, that I can unlock my luks encrypted drive with my fido2 token, but forgot the passphrase. I tried to get the key with gdb, but the breakpoint `crypt_activate_by_volume_key` did not work for me. @L11R What did you use as the breakpoint? Also the binary is stripped, how did you print the key or do you have compiled it with debug symbols for that?
@mo-pyy I used CLion to debug it. Just cloned this repo and started debug. As the breakpoint I used the line I highlighed in the comment above. You need to watch `base64_encoded` variable.
I did not use CLion before, how do I configure the run / debug configuration?

As the previous comment https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/20230#issuecomment-956570905, @L11R found the base64 encoded key, which is used as an argument to `crypt_activate_by_passphrase`. So you need to set the breakpoint to `crypt_activate_by_passphrase`, not `crypt_activate_by_volume_key` which I wrote wrongly.
Can someone write all the steps down with the commands for a debugging noob like me? Thanks.
#25777 addresses this for fido2 tokens (but not for pkcs11 yet)

Since cryptsetup 2.6.0, you can use `cryptsetup luksAddKey --token-type systemd-fido/systemd-tpm2` to add a password to luks with fido/tpm, then you can operate normally.

review_comments: otoh dropping these three certainly makes sense afaics.

Please do not drop `friendly_name` here. We really should include that in the PIN prompt. The fact that we currently do not is an omission we should fix.

i.e. instead of dropping this parameter please change the ask_password_auto() line above to include it in the question, so that it is clear for which volume we need the token.

and the `name` should not be dropped either, but passed in the `id` parameter of ask_password_auto() (i.e. the third one, which is currently NULL), so that agents implementing the passwword question protocol can identify what we are asking for.
What name do you think we should pass in from cryptenroll? Or maybe just make it NULL in that case only?

It seems that none of the other cryptsetup modes included the volume name / friendly name in their calls to ask_password_auto() either. I'll just leave this change out of this PR and potentially fix it in a future one.
Do we need _INVALID here though? Because `arg_unlock_type` defaults to `UNLOCK_PASSWORD` anyway, and _INVALID will never be used.
either use `free_and_replace()` or place `assert(!arg_unlock_fido2_device)` here to indicate that you verified that the variable could not possibly be initialized before.
